steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with the molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths of visible light, particularly blue light, are scattered much more effectively than longer wavelengths like red or yellow, causing blue light to be dispersed in all directions across the sky. When you look at any part of the sky (away from the sun), your eyes receive this scattered blue light, making the entire sky appear blue.
